entities.summary:
Zhao Lei was a military officer serving under the warlord Liu Bei in the late Eastern Han dynasty.

Born in 179 AD, Zhao Lei rose through the ranks of the Han army, becoming a trusted advisor to Liu Bei.

During the reign of Emperor Ling, Zhao Lei played a key role in several key battles against the warlord Dong Zhuo, including the Battle of Luchou and the Battle of Xiapi.

After Liu Bei's death in 220 AD, Zhao Lei continued to serve under his successor, Cao Pi, before eventually retreating to the mountains to escape the chaos of the Three Kingdoms period.

Despite his relatively minor status in the grand scheme of the Three Kingdoms, Zhao Lei's actions had a lasting impact on the region, cementing his place in the annals of Chinese military history.

The story of Zhao Lei serves as a testament to the bravery and loyalty of the Han army, and his legacy continues to be celebrated by historians and enthusiasts alike.

Zhao Lei's significance lies in his ability to adapt to the changing political landscape of the late Eastern Han, and his role in shaping the fate of the warlord Liu Bei.

In the words of the great historian Sima Qian, 'Zhao Lei's bravery and loyalty were an inspiration to his comrades, and his actions will always be remembered as a shining example of the virtues of the Han dynasty.'

This passage is a tribute to the enduring legacy of Zhao Lei, a man who, despite his relatively minor status, left an indelible mark on the course of Chinese history.
